findings.text: non-blocking: _paths_present_in_tree duplicates a capability the repository already owns — reckon/velocity.py:337 _tree_paths lists every tracked path at a revision with one ls-tree -r --name-only, and the public read_blobs at reckon/velocity.py:409 answers which (revision, path) specs the object store holds, returning None for a missing one. The addition neither extends nor imports either owner, so the reuse dimension scores 5 under the rubric; the divergence is deliberate in one respect only (it returns None rather than raising when the probe cannot answer), which could have been a thin wrapper over read_blobs.

non-blocking: _write_suite_manifest is defined twice in the new test file, identically at line 145 and again at line 361; the second definition shadows the first, so seven lines are dead and a later edit to one copy silently has no effect on the tests that call it.

non-blocking: the per-tree rule reaches dispatch but not repair briefs. _reviewed_run_suite_command resolves the reviewed run's template over the whole write scope and hands the repair both its done-when text (repair.py:645 'run with exactly <resolved list>') and its recorded suite_command, so the repair's record carries no {node_test_files} placeholder; _arm_missing_fields therefore takes its unscoped branch and promotion compares the repair's arm command literally. A repair of a scope whose test set changed is now refused either way — running the inherited list exits 4 over a deleted file (collected_no_test) and resolving per tree fails command_matches_suite_command — where before the change the same pair promoted silently. The file is outside this node's write scope; the landed collected-nothing refusal is what makes the gap observable.
